issues.claim: "Reviews there complain about unreturned calls." (Section 1, Now)
issues.problem: Generalization from a small visible sample. Only one of the five review cards visible on the cited Yahoo Local page explicitly describes unreturned calls (08/19/25 reviewer: called repeatedly, manager would not take or return the call). The other visible reviews concern manager availability, receptionist tone and general competence. The Yelp full-text and Google review corpus (206 reviews) could not be opened, and independent search providers were rate-limited during this check, so a plural 'reviews' pattern could not be confirmed. Claim is partly supported, not false.
issues.fix: Narrow the wording to what the page shows, e.g. "A recent review describes repeated calls never returned" or "several reviews describe phone and callback problems."

issues.claim: "new portal accounts take two business days to approve" (Section 1, Now)
issues.problem: The portal page promises a staff review and a reply 'within 2 business days'; it does not state that approval itself completes in two days. 'Approve' overstates the sourced language.
issues.fix: Say "new portal access requests are reviewed by staff, who promise a reply within two business days."

issues.claim: Section 1 Impact: "1.5-6 staff hours a week"
issues.problem: Ambiguous unit. The underlying analysis (and the arithmetic: 10-20 hrs x 15-30%) is per piloted community, but the sentence reads as a total across 'piloted communities'. A reader could take the range as covering all 3-5 pilot sites.
issues.fix: Add "per piloted community": "1.5-6 staff hours a week per community, $2.4k-$9.7k a year per community."

issues.problem: Unlike sections 1 and 3, no wage basis or time unit is stated. The dollars imply roughly $24/hour (the NJ median for Secretaries and Administrative Assistants in the analysis), and the amount is not labelled per year. Arithmetic itself reproduces (5,000 x 4 min = 333 hrs; 10,000 x 8 min = 1,333 hrs).
issues.fix: Add the basis and the unit: "...330-1,330 staff hours a year, or $8k-$32k a year at an assumed ~$24/hour administrative cost."

issues.claim: "offices are open weekdays 9-5 per your public listing" (Section 1, Now)
issues.problem: The hours come from a third-party Yahoo Local/Yelp-sourced listing, not from RCP's own site (the contact page publishes addresses and phones but no hours). 'Your public listing' implies the company's own listing.
issues.fix: Attribute it plainly: "weekday 9-5 hours per your Yelp/Yahoo Local listing."

issues.claim: "the study behind the band brackets 14% and 34%" (Section 1, Impact)
issues.problem: The figures are correct (NBER WP 31161: 14% average, 34% for novice/low-skilled agents), but the study is not identified as customer-support research. Left unlabelled, it can read as a property-management benchmark.
issues.fix: Add three words of context: "the customer-support study behind the band brackets 14% and 34%."

issues.claim: Walk-in opener: "I work with New Jersey community managers on callback backlogs and work-order paperwork"
issues.problem: This is a claim about our own client base, not about RCP, so no public source can verify it. Nothing in profile.json, analysis.json or industry.json documents existing NJ community-management clients. If it is not true, it is a misrepresentation in a first-contact walk-in.
issues.fix: Confirm against our own client list before use; if we have no NJ community-management clients, change to "I build AI helpers for New Jersey property and community managers" or similar.

issues.claim: Email: "lists preparing work orders, entering them and back-charging owner accounts by hand"
issues.problem: 'By hand' is our characterization, not the posting's language. The posting does describe the steps as manual duties (prepare work orders, enter all work orders into system, back charge owner accounts), so the substance holds; the phrase is only a mild overstatement.
issues.fix: Low priority. Optionally soften to "lists preparing and entering work orders and back-charging owner accounts as part of the job."
